title: Spring lawn and garden checklist for Greater Victoria

seo.title: Spring Lawn & Garden Checklist for Greater Victoria
seo.description: A practical list of spring lawn, bed and pruning tasks suited to Greater Victoria's coastal climate, plus the local rules to know before you start.

summary: What to do in your lawn and beds from March to May on southern Vancouver Island.

body.p: Spring comes early on southern Vancouver Island. Lawns start growing in March, and beds wake up weeks earlier than in most of Canada. A little work now saves a lot in summer, when the CRD lawn watering schedule limits how much water you can use.

list: Rake out winter debris and look for moss. Moss usually points to shade, compaction or poor drainage, not just a lack of fertilizer.
Aerate compacted areas once the soil is moist but not waterlogged.
Overseed thin patches in April or May while the ground is cool and damp.
Start mowing high. Taller grass shades its roots and copes better with dry summers.
In deep shade under big firs or cedars, consider a mulched bed of native groundcover instead of lawn.
Clear weeds before they set seed.
Cut back last year's perennial stems once new growth shows.
Top up mulch to hold moisture into summer.
Plant new perennials and shrubs early so roots grow before the dry months.
Prune summer-flowering shrubs in early spring.
Wait until after flowering for spring bloomers like rhododendron, forsythia and lilac.

Check hedges and trees for active nests before cutting. B.C.'s Wildlife Act protects any bird's nest while it holds a bird or egg, and the nests of eagles, ospreys, herons, peregrine falcons, gyrfalcons and burrowing owls all year; federal law also protects migratory birds' nests.

body.p: Start up your system and check every zone before CRD Stage 1 rules begin on May 1. See our [irrigation start-up and winterization guide](/resources/irrigation-start-up-and-winterization/) and the [CRD watering rules guide](/resources/crd-watering-rules-guide/).

Check your municipality's tree rules before you prune hard or remove a tree. Our [winter pruning guide](/resources/winter-pruning-and-storm-prep/) explains what they usually cover, and each [area page](/areas/) links to the local bylaw.
Want this handled for you? [Get a free quote](/quote/) for [grounds maintenance](/services/grounds-maintenance/).
Watering and tree rules can change between seasons. Check the sources linked below and your municipality before you start. This checklist was prepared in November 2026.
